items.title: Self-Building Labs
items.snippet: This study introduces the concept of Self-Building Labs, focusing on automated scientific discovery. It integrates AI and robotics to accelerate experimental processes and data generation, representing a significant step towards autonomous research environments. The paper highlights the potential for AI-driven systems to design and execute experiments with minimal human intervention.

items.title: Leaner Training, Lower Leakage: Revisiting Memorization in LLM Fine-Tuning with LoRA
items.snippet: This research explores the impact of LoRA on memorization in fine-tuned Large Language Models, aiming for more efficient training with reduced leakage. The study re-examines the phenomenon of memorization, proposing methods to mitigate unintended data retention. It provides insights into optimizing LLM fine-tuning processes for better privacy and efficiency.

items.title: Characterizing Recoverable Expert-Utilization Signatures in Fine-Tuned Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
items.snippet: The paper investigates structural memory vulnerabilities in fine-tuned Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models. It proposes methods to recover expert paths through routing and output logits, aiding in the detection of targeted attacks. This work contributes to understanding and securing complex LLM architectures.

items.title: MoLRSI: A Recursive Self-Improving AI agent for Molecular Discovery
items.snippet: This study introduces MoLRSI, an intelligent agent designed for molecular discovery, optimizing workflow and model architecture. It integrates cross-task memory for enhanced performance in applications like antibiotic discovery and peptide-MHC binding agent design. The agent's recursive self-improving nature promises accelerated breakthroughs in chemical research.

items.title: Optimizing Stochastic Policy Geometry for Few-Step Flow Reinforcement Learning
items.snippet: The research proposes the Geo-FSRL method to enhance the performance of few-step flow reinforcement learning. It demonstrates superior results in image and video generation tasks under a 4-step setting compared to existing methods. This optimization focuses on improving the efficiency and effectiveness of reinforcement learning algorithms.

items.title: BlindToChange: AI Agents Can Find Changes When Asked But Do They Look When Needed?
items.snippet: This paper explores the behavior of AI agents in detecting changes, questioning whether they actively seek out changes or only respond when prompted. It delves into the underlying mechanisms of change detection in AI systems, highlighting implications for agent autonomy and perception. The research investigates the proactive versus reactive nature of AI agents.

items.title: agent-desktop
items.snippet: Agent Desktop enables reliable computer use for any AI agent on the desktop. Built with Rust, it leverages OS accessibility trees to perceive UI structure and execute actions safely and stably, rather than relying on pixel-based inferences. This tool aims to enhance the autonomy and robustness of AI agents interacting with graphical user interfaces.

items.title: claude-mem
items.snippet: This project provides persistent context across sessions for AI agents, capturing and compressing agent activities with AI. It injects relevant context into future sessions, supporting various models like Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Gemini. The goal is to improve long-term memory and coherence for AI agent interactions.

items.title: Scrapling
items.snippet: Scrapling is a web scraping framework that manages everything from single requests to full-scale crawls. It provides robust tools for undetected browser automation using stealth Firefox, Python, and anti-bot measures, making it ideal for large-scale data collection. This framework aims to simplify and enhance web scraping capabilities.

items.title: Claude-Code-Game-Studios
items.snippet: This repository transforms Claude Code into a comprehensive game development studio, featuring 49 AI agents and 72 workflow skills. It implements a complete coordination system that mirrors real studio hierarchies for efficient game creation. The project showcases advanced multi-agent collaboration in a creative domain.

items.title: FreeToken
items.snippet: FreeToken enables datacenter-scale model serving directly on your desktop, allowing massive models to run locally with high speed and efficiency. This project aims to democratize access to powerful AI models for local execution without relying on cloud infrastructure. It addresses the challenge of running large models on consumer-grade hardware.

items.title: roboskills
items.snippet: Roboskills provides a minimal set of agent workflows and tools specifically designed for robotics applications. It enables coding agents like Claude Code or Codex to perform robotics tasks through integrated skills and tools that wrap existing models. The project aims to simplify the development and deployment of AI agents in robotic systems.

items.title: llm-daily-review
items.snippet: This repository automates the daily discovery and evaluation of LLM applications from Hacker News. It scrapes submissions, tests each in an isolated Docker container, and scores them across 11 criteria, publishing results and weekly newsletters. The project offers a systematic approach to identifying and assessing new LLM tools.

items.title: What is Super Intelligence?
items.snippet: NASA defines Artificial Intelligence as a machine-based system that makes predictions, recommendations, or decisions for human-defined objectives, influencing real or virtual environments. Super Intelligence tools at NASA often use machine learning to train computers for classifications, predictions, or uncovering trends in large datasets. Common methods include decision support tools that consider multiple outcomes and probabilities in complex, imperfect situations.

dropped.snippet: Genie 4 offers unprecedented realism, advanced physics, lifelike human movement, and native audio for real-time interactive simulation. dropped.snippet: nanochat is presented as 'the best ChatGPT that $100 can buy,' offering an efficient and cost-effective solution for conversational AI. dropped.title: UC San Diego Launches AI-Driven Chip Design Research Initiative Supported By Qualcomm Technologies
dropped.snippet: UC San Diego has launched a new AI-driven chip design research initiative, supported by a $500,000 gift from Qualcomm Technologies. This collaboration aims to rethink how next-generation computing systems and systems-on-chips are designed, applying AI to optimize processing speed, energy consumption, and memory capacity. Researchers will explore new architectures and predict performance to accelerate innovation in semiconductor design.

dropped.title: College Students Use AI Extensively, Survey Shows
dropped.snippet: A new 2026 Dartmouth AI Survey reveals widespread AI usage among college students across the nation and their views on AI's impact on jobs. The survey indicates that most students use AI tools for tasks like explaining concepts, summarizing readings, and solving math problems. Fifty percent of students acknowledge peers use AI text with little editing, highlighting concerns about fairness in take-home work.

dropped.snippet: The EPSRC AI and Robotics team plays a key role in engaging with UKRI colleagues and the research communities to maintain the UK's leading position in AI and robotics research. They collaborate with engineering and ICT themes to set strategic direction and support the development of core capabilities. Recent investments include new AI hubs addressing foundational mathematics and computational research, as well as AI for science, engineering, and real-world data applications.

dropped.title: Proton's AI manifesto for software engineering
dropped.snippet: Proton's manifesto argues that the engineer's role has fundamentally shifted from writing code to helping LLMs write better code faster. Engineers are now team leaders managing models and agents, tasked with guiding and correcting them. The manifesto emphasizes pushing the limits of LLM autonomy, identifying problems LLMs can't solve, and continuously improving workflows and shared resources for all.
